intro: You are auditing a fleet of {n} server hosts for configuration drift; the audit date is {date}. Each host has one of eight roles (web, api, db, cache, worker, gateway, batch, search), and each role has a baseline of required key = value settings. A host's configuration is spread over several files, and approved exceptions allow specific deviations until an expiry date. Your job: for every host, find every baseline key whose effective value deviates from the role baseline and is not covered by a valid exception, and say why.
rules: A host's effective configuration is built from its files whose names end in .conf, read in lexical (sorted) order of their full paths; within and across files a later line for the same key overrides an earlier one. Files with any other ending (for example .conf.disabled) are ignored.
Lines starting with # are comments and are ignored; blank lines are ignored. A setting line has the form key = value; leading and trailing spaces around the value do not count.
Only keys listed in the host's role baseline are audited. A baseline key with no setting line in any .conf file is MISSING.

A baseline key whose effective value differs from the baseline value is a deviation. An exception applies to a host if its target is that host's name or role:<the host's role>. An exception is valid if its expiry date is on or after the audit date.

A deviation is covered (not reported) if a valid exception for that key has exactly the effective value. Otherwise report it with one reason: EXPIRED if an applicable exception for that key has exactly the effective value but has expired; MISMATCH if there is no such exception but a valid applicable exception for that key names a different value; UNAPPROVED otherwise. Exceptions for other hosts or other roles never apply.
file_headers: # This file is managed by the central configuration management system; do not edit by hand.
# Manual edits will be overwritten at the next configuration management run.
# Generated automatically from the fleet configuration repository; local changes are not preserved.
# Hand-made changes here are reverted without notice.
# Configuration owned by the team that operates this host.
# Direct questions about this file to the service owner on call.
# Changes to this file require sign-off from the owning team.
# The owning team reviews this file at every scheduled audit.
# All changes must go through the change-control process before deployment.
# Do not modify this file outside an approved change window.
# Emergency edits must be recorded in the change log afterwards.
# Deviations from the role baseline require an approved exception.
justifications: Temporary mitigation for an active incident
Workaround for a known memory leak
Canary analysis for a planned rollout
Workaround for a kernel scheduling defect
Baseline value triggers a scanner false positive
Capacity trial ahead of peak season
Upgrade blocked by a downstream dependency

tools.list_hosts: Lists the hosts of the fleet as 'host name | role' lines, paged, returning at most 200 hosts per call.
tools.list_files: Lists the configuration file paths of one host.
tools.read_file: Returns the text of one file of one host.
tools.get_baseline: Returns the baseline key = value list of one role.
tools.get_exceptions: Returns all exceptions whose target is the given host or its role, each with id, target, key = value, expiry date and justification.

answer: The final answer is plain lines, one finding per line, in the literal form <host> | <key> | <reason>, where reason is one of UNAPPROVED, EXPIRED, MISMATCH, MISSING; for example web-use1-0007 | app.log_level | UNAPPROVED. Hosts without findings are left out. Lines in any other form are ignored.
score: The score is the F1 score of the finding lines against the true findings.
